name: Geshur
overview: Geshur was a district located east of the Jordan River, remaining unconquered by the Israelites as indicated in Joshua 13:2. The region and its inhabitants were distinct from the Philistine and Canaanite territories, as seen in the listing of lands and peoples surrounding it (Joshua 13:3-6). The biblical narrative highlights the significance of Geshur through its association with David, who married a princess from this area, and through Absalom, who sought refuge there after the murder of Amnon, underscoring both its political and familial importance in Israel's history.
